sections.content: An adjective comes directly before the noun it describes, and it stays in its plain dictionary form there -- it never takes a case ending or changes for number. Any case or number ending goes on the noun, not the adjective.

Because the adjective doesn't change, 'nagy méret' and 'nagy pólók' both keep nagy exactly the same. Only when an adjective stands alone as the predicate, like 'A póló piros' (the T-shirt is red), does it behave differently -- that's a separate pattern.
